name: Calendar
description: A personal calendar: a Rust (axum) API and a React single-page app shipped in one container, backed by PostgreSQL, with Google sign-in for allow-listed people. The API serves events, tasks and day/week agendas; the web app shows day, week, task and overdue-triage views. Significant decisions of any kind are recorded as ADRs (any decision records) in docs/decisions and published on the documentation site.

contract-first.description: The OpenAPI document is the contract between the backend and every UI. The API build writes it, CI fails when the committed copy is stale, and the TypeScript client is generated from it and never hand-edited (ADR-0004).

config.format: OpenAPI 3, code-first: utoipa collects the paths and schemas, and calendar-api/src/openapi.rs rewrites them into the dialect of the committed contract (calendar-api --openapi)
config.staleness-gate: CI job Backend: the calendar-api test contract::the_committed_contract_is_what_the_api_generates (byte-exact against contracts/openapi.json); the frontend typecheck fails on a contract break

quality-gates.description: Every change passes the same gates locally (just check) and in CI: analyzers and Clippy with warnings as errors, formatting, type-aware lint, tests (including the check that the migrated schema matches schema.rs), the contract check, the tooling tests and the ADR conventions check. The single required status check on main is 'CI result' (ADR-0009, ADR-0012, ADR-0036).

config.entry-point: just check (= just lint + just test)
backend-checks: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings (clippy::all denied, clippy::pedantic on, unsafe forbidden)
cargo fetch --locked and --locked on every build, with the toolchain pinned in backend/rust-toolchain.toml
cargo test (infrastructure and API tests on Testcontainers PostgreSQL; the translated migrations are compared with the schema EF Core produced)
contracts/openapi.json regenerated and compared with the committed file
frontend-checks: Vitest + Testing Library + MSW (unhandled requests fail tests)
Docs site build verified at the root path and at a project subpath
repository-checks: just tools test (tests and analyzers of every .NET file-based tool, shellcheck for doctor.sh)
just tools versions (tool package pins match backend)
just tools adr (MADR front matter, section order, rating tables, driver coverage, links, index)
just --list --list-submodules and just --fmt --check on the justfile and each module file (*.just)
Container image build + smoke test against PostgreSQL in Docker
Azure role SQL matches the local init script
security-scanning: CodeQL security-extended (csharp, javascript-typescript, actions) on push, PR and weekly
Dependency review fails on moderate+ vulnerabilities
Dependabot for NuGet, npm, Docker and Actions
config.merge-gate: Ruleset on main: PR required, 'CI result' must pass, no high+ CodeQL alerts, no force-push or deletion, squash/rebase only

supply-chain-integrity.description: Builds are reproducible from pinned toolchains and lock files, base images and third-party actions are pinned by digest or SHA, dependency updates are automated, and deployment uses OIDC federation rather than long-lived credentials (ADR-0053, ADR-0010, ADR-0012, ADR-0034).

toolchain-pins: .NET SDK 10.0.300 or later for repo tools, whose #:include needs it (ADR-0017), verified by just doctor
Azure CLI and Bicep versions in tools/azure-versions.env, verified by just doctor
lockfiles: backend/*/packages.lock.json (NuGet CPM + source mapping to nuget.org)
config.base-image-pinning: Dockerfile pins the node, rust and distroless cc images by sha256 digest; compose.yaml pins postgres:18.6-alpine (single source of truth for Testcontainers)
config.action-pinning: GitHub-owned actions by major tag, third-party actions by commit SHA
config.deployment-credentials: GitHub Actions OIDC federation to a per-environment Azure identity (issuer token.actions.githubusercontent.com, audience api://AzureADTokenExchange, subject repo:mgasca/calendar:environment:<env>); no stored Azure secrets

environment-separation.description: Staging and production are separate Azure resource groups with their own Container App, PostgreSQL server, Key Vaults, Google OAuth client, allow-list and deployment identity. Staging holds synthetic data only (ADR-0035).

config.isolation-unit: Azure resource group per environment with its own user-assigned identity, Container Apps environment, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, app and ops Key Vaults, Container Registry, Log Analytics workspace and Google OAuth client
shared-resources: None at the Azure level; the GitHub repository and its workflows are shared
config.promotion: The same SHA-tagged image is deployed to staging first; production deployment requires reviewer approval of the GitHub 'production' environment (ADR-0034). Deployment is currently run with `just infra deploy <env>` (tools/infra, Bicep); migrations with the 'Database migration' workflow.

nodes.name: Calendar user
nodes.description: A person whose verified Google email is on the allow-list. Uses the web app in a browser to see today and the week, add events and tasks, tick tasks off and triage overdue tasks.

nodes.name: Maintainer / operator
nodes.description: The repository owner who merges pull requests, deploys infrastructure with the infra tool, initialises secrets and roles, runs database migrations and approves production deployments.

nodes.name: Google Identity (OpenID Connect)
nodes.description: External identity provider. The API runs the OpenID Connect authorization-code flow against it; the browser is redirected to Google to sign in and back to the API callback with a code.

metadata.per-environment: A separate OAuth client (client id, secret and redirect URI) per environment (ADR-0035)

nodes.name: Calendar system
nodes.description: The whole product: web app, API, generated client, contract, database, migrator and documentation site, all developed in the single repository mgasca/calendar.

nodes.name: Calendar web app
nodes.description: React 19 + Vite + TypeScript single-page app (frontend/apps/web). TanStack Router with code-based routes for /, /day/$date, /week, /week/$weekStart, /tasks, /triage and /signin; TanStack Query for server state. Reads the browser's IANA time zone and local date and sends them with every agenda request. Served as static files from the API container (same origin, no CORS).

interfaces.description: Same origin as the API; in development Vite proxies /api to http://localhost:5041. Under just frontend dev-signed-in the proxy adds the Development-only X-Dev-Seed-Key to /api requests from the app's own origin only (Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin checked), only towards a loopback API and only while vite or vite preview listens on loopback (--host is refused), so the browser is signed in without Google and never sees the key (ADR-0027 amendment, story 0021)

client-performance.description: Rules from the frontend performance review (issues #42–#49): cache server state for 30 s, refetch agendas every 5 minutes and on focus/visibility/midnight, update task toggles optimistically with per-task rollback, cache Intl formatters, subscribe to the clock only in the smallest component, and prove every performance fix with a test that fails without it.

config.optimistic-updates: Task complete/reopen only (useToggleTask): patch the cached view, roll back only that task on failure, refetch once after the last in-flight toggle settles or immediately after an error. Event and task creation are not optimistic.
config.formatter-caching: dateTimeFormat(locale, options) in features/agenda/dayTime.ts caches Intl.DateTimeFormat instances; never construct one in a comparator
config.clock-subscriptions: useNow() only in components showing minute-sensitive state; useToday(zone) when only the date matters; one shared timer
config.code-splitting: /tasks, /triage and /week/$weekStart routes are lazy (createLazyRoute); measured gain ~2% of the entry chunk; triage chunk 5.54 kB
config.evidence: Every fix needs a test that fails without it (React Profiler render count, MSW request counter or vi.spyOn call count); say whether a finding is measured or inferred

accessibility.description: Accessibility and usability acceptance criteria shared by the story cards: keyboard operation, native modal dialogs with focus management, status messages for assistive tech, overdue conveyed in text as well as colour, and usable loading/empty/error states on a phone.

keyboard: Week view: ← / → move a week, t goes to this week; ignored in fields, editable text or with a modifier
Week grid is a focusable 'Week grid' region where arrows scroll
Every control is reachable and operable by keyboard; duplicate submission is blocked while an action is pending
dialogs: Native <dialog> via the shared ModalDialog component
Focus moves to the first field on open, is trapped while open and returns to the opener on close
Cancel/Escape close without a discard prompt; both do nothing while saving
The dialog reopens fresh without previous values
Deletion requires a ConfirmDialog stating the task count (hard delete, no undo)
config.status-messages: Confirmations use role="status" (e.g. 'Dentist added for Thu 29 Oct' with a Show day link); form errors use a single role="alert"
config.colour: Overdue and past-due are conveyed in text as well as colour
config.landmarks: Each day is a <section aria-labelledby>; hidden '+N more' events stay in the accessible list
config.theme: Switchable light and dark themes: semantic CSS tokens from @calendar/theme selected by a data-theme attribute, following the system until the user picks one (story 0039, ADR-0047); plain CSS, no component library (adding one needs an ADR)
config.small-screens: Day, task and triage views usable on a phone; the week grid scrolls sideways (no mobile layout yet)

metadata.runtime: Browser; React 19, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, openapi-fetch

nodes.name: @calendar/api-client
nodes.description: TypeScript package (frontend/packages/api-client) generated from contracts/openapi.json with openapi-typescript; createApiClient wraps openapi-fetch with the typed paths. schema.gen.ts is never hand-edited. Shared by every TypeScript UI so that no UI depends on backend code.

nodes.name: @calendar/theme
nodes.description: TypeScript and CSS package (frontend/packages/theme) shared by the web app and the documentation site: the semantic colour tokens for the light and dark themes, selected by a data-theme attribute with a prefers-color-scheme fallback (tokens.css), the self-hosted Fontsource variable fonts (fonts.css), and the stored theme choice (THEME_STORAGE_KEY, isThemeChoice). Its tests check token contrast and that no colour literal escapes the token layer.

nodes.name: OpenAPI contract
nodes.description: contracts/openapi.json: the committed OpenAPI 3 document emitted by the API build. It is the single contract between the backend and every client; CI fails when it is stale.

nodes.name: Calendar API
nodes.description: axum API in Rust (backend/crates/calendar-api) with a framework-free calendar-domain crate (time-zone and day-inclusion rules) and calendar-infrastructure (Diesel over diesel-async on tokio-postgres, SQL forms of the domain rules). Serves events, tasks, day and week agenda read models and Google sign-in with a cookie session; also serves the SPA's static files and index.html fallback. Every endpoint requires an authenticated user except health and sign-in.

interfaces.description: The axum server on tokio listens on http://+:8080 inside the container (ASPNETCORE_URLS, set in the image; http://localhost:5041 when unset); TLS terminates at the Container Apps ingress

interfaces.authentication: login and callback anonymous; me and logout require the session cookie

interfaces.description: Development only: the OpenAPI document with the request's origin as its server URL. The route is not registered outside Development; the committed contracts/openapi.json comes from calendar-api --openapi
Static files from wwwroot (the built SPA); unknown non-file, non-/api paths return index.html with 200 and Cache-Control: no-cache; unknown /api/* paths return 404

interfaces.image: crcalendar<suffix>.azurecr.io/calendar:<git-sha> (built from Dockerfile; gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13 runtime, non-root user)

authentication.description: Google OpenID Connect with a backend-for-frontend cookie session (ADR-0027). The fallback authorization policy requires an authenticated user on every endpoint; only health, the sign-in endpoints and the SPA static files are anonymous. Only verified emails on the allow-list may sign in.

config.identity-provider: Google OpenID Connect (authorization-code flow with state, PKCE and nonce in calendar-api), callback /api/auth/callback/google
config.pattern: Backend-for-frontend: the API holds the OAuth client secret and issues a same-origin cookie; the browser never sees tokens
config.fallback-policy: Every handler outside health, sign-in and the static files takes a CurrentUser extractor, which answers 401 or 403 and never redirects (calendar-api/src/auth.rs)
anonymous-endpoints: SPA static files and index.html fallback

allow-list.source: Auth:AllowedEmails (Key Vault secrets allowed-email-N → Auth__AllowedEmails__N in Azure; .env locally)
allow-list.comparison: case-insensitive exact match; failure redirects to /signin?error=access_denied without creating a session

session-cookie.secure: Always outside Development; in Development only when the request came over HTTPS
session-cookie.key-storage: One 32-byte key in the session_keys table of the database, created by the API on first use; it seals the stateless session cookie (XChaCha20-Poly1305)

config.open-redirect-protection: returnUrl must be a local absolute path (no //, no backslash, no control characters) on both server (ApiAuthentication.LocalReturnUrl) and client (safeReturnTo)
config.unauthenticated-api-response: 401 (or 403) for /api/* instead of a redirect; the client raises calendar:unauthorized and routes to /signin with the current URL

per-user-data-isolation.description: Every event and task belongs to one user (owner_id). Every event and task repository function takes the signed-in user's OwnerId and builds its query from queries::owned_events / owned_tasks, so every read, count and set-based update or delete is scoped; another user's id answers 404 (ADR-0041).

config.owner-column: events.owner_id and tasks.owner_id: non-null uuid, FOREIGN KEY users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
config.identity-key: users keyed by Google's sub claim (unique), email lower-cased and unique; resolved or created at the Google callback (calendar_infrastructure::users::resolve): by subject, else by email among rows without a subject, else the unclaimed legacy placeholder for the first allow-listed email, else a new row
config.scoping-mechanism: Every event and task repository function takes an OwnerId (the user id in the session) and builds its query from queries::owned_events / owned_tasks, which start with the owner predicate; an insert refuses a row owned by anyone else
config.fail-closed: There is no ambient user: a request without one never reaches a repository, because the CurrentUser extractor rejects it first, and no repository function runs without an OwnerId. Only the migrator (as calendar_migrator) and tests read the tables directly
config.legacy-owner: The per_user_ownership migration inserts users row 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 and backfills every existing event and task to it; the first sign-in or seed run by Auth:AllowedEmails[0] claims it
config.session-claim: The users.id travels in the sealed session ticket; a ticket without one is rejected with 401 and the cookie cleared (calendar-api/src/auth.rs, ADR-0056), so sessions issued before ADR-0041 end once
config.cross-user-response: 404 for GET/PUT/DELETE /api/events/{id}, GET/PUT/complete/reopen/DELETE /api/tasks/{id}; notFound outcome in POST /api/tasks/bulk by ids; filter-based bulk actions and agenda counts only ever cover the caller's rows

time-correctness.description: The client's IANA time zone and local date define the day; the server never decides what day it is (ADR-0021). Instants are UTC with an end-exclusive span plus the IANA zone id, all-day values are end-exclusive floating dates, and DST gaps and overlaps are handled in one place (ADR-0057).

config.day-defined-by: The client: every endpoint that judges overdue or upcoming takes today/date + timeZone, validated with FieldErrors::require_date / require_time_zone (calendar-api/src/validation.rs) and marked required in OpenAPI
config.time-zone-ids: IANA only; legacy aliases mapped to canonical ids from tzdata's backward table (calendar-domain time/iana_aliases.rs); '+' must be sent as %2B
config.instants: DateTimeOffset with an explicit offset (ExplicitOffsetConverter; missing offset → 400), normalised to UTC and stored as timestamptz; tasks have DueDate XOR DueAt (check constraint ck_tasks_due_date_xor_due_at)
config.floating-dates: DateOnly stored as date; all-day events are [startDate, endDate) end-exclusive
config.date-range: Years 1900–2200 (ADR-0024); anything else is 400 on the API and notFound in the router

dst.non-existent-local-time: Rejected on the client (deadlineInstants / event form) and server
dst.ambiguous-local-time: The user chooses the occurrence (UTC offset)
dst.skipped-date: An empty day window (e.g. Pacific/Apia 2011-12-30); the week view shows a note
dst.day-window: DayWindow: [local midnight D, local midnight D+1) as UTC; 23 h and 25 h days handled; a non-existent midnight starts at the first valid instant

config.server-clock: Injected Clock (SystemClock in the app, a fixed test clock in tests), used only to stamp completedAt

read-consistency.description: Every agenda read (day or week) is one read-only REPEATABLE READ snapshot, so a task completed or an event added between its queries cannot appear in some lists and not others (ADR-0020). The week endpoint reuses the same range-based builder with the same fixed number of queries (ADR-0024).

config.queries-per-read: Four range queries (all-day events, timed events, due tasks, overdue tasks + two counts) whatever the range length; each loads plain Diesel row structs, no N+1
config.single-rule-implementation: calendar_domain::agenda::day_inclusion decides per-day membership in memory; calendar_infrastructure::queries holds the SQL forms; the agreement tests (agenda_agreement, week_agenda_agreement) prove they agree, and a week/day agreement test proves days[i] of a week equals the day agenda

concurrency-control.description: Writes use optimistic concurrency on the PostgreSQL xmin system column (ADR-0052) and report conflicts as 409. Set-based bulk actions on 'all N overdue' run in a SERIALIZABLE transaction guarded by the client's expected count.

config.token: xmin (xid) concurrency token on events and tasks, read and compared only in calendar-infrastructure; PUT /api/events/{id} and PUT /api/tasks/{id} require the client's version from the response and answer 409 when it is stale
idempotent-operations: DELETE /api/tasks/{id} (404 treated as already deleted by the client)

bulk-filtered-writes.guard: The open-overdue count for the client's today/timeZone must equal filter.expectedTotal
bulk-filtered-writes.on-mismatch: Roll back and return 409 'The overdue task count changed'; serialization failures and deadlocks also map to 409

config.client-behaviour: A 409 on a toggle triggers a refetch; the triage view asks the user to review the new count and retry; per-id bulk results report applied, skipped or notFound

request-limits.description: All input is validated into RFC 9457 problem details with per-field errors; list endpoints use opaque keyset cursors with bounded page sizes; bulk requests are capped.

config.error-format: application/problem+json (RFC 9457); binding failures become 400 via BadRequestExceptionHandler

pagination.style: Keyset, every comparison in SQL, limit + 1 fetched to detect the next page
pagination.cursor: Opaque base64url JSON tied to its view

observability.description: The container exposes /api/health for startup, liveness and readiness probes; console logs and probe results go to the Log Analytics workspace, and Application Insights is provisioned in the same workspace. Decided, not yet delivered (ADR-0062, story 0064): the API and the web app emit OpenTelemetry over OTLP to Grafana LGTM locally and in E2E and, for the API, to Application Insights in Azure, under an attribute allow-list that keeps personal data out; every end-to-end flow test asserts its trace, logs, metrics and the absence of personal data.

config.health-endpoint: GET /api/health → { "status": "ok" } (anonymous; starts without a database connection string)
config.logs: Container Apps appLogsConfiguration → Log Analytics workspace law-calendar-<suffix>
config.telemetry: The Container Apps environment runs the managed OpenTelemetry agent (appInsightsConfiguration and openTelemetryConfiguration in infra/modules/app.bicep): it receives the API's OTLP over gRPC and sends traces and logs to Application Insights appi-calendar-<suffix> (workspace-based); the app sets OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=calendar-api and OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none, request metrics come from the Container Apps platform metrics, and the API's console output still reaches Log Analytics (#738)
audit-logs: Key Vault AuditEvent diagnostics for the app and ops vaults
config.structured-logging: tracing with tracing-subscriber's formatter at INFO, written to standard output

telemetry-decision.standard: OpenTelemetry over OTLP, configured only by OTEL_* variables; no exporter when no endpoint is set
signals: API: one server span per request named '<METHOD> <route template>', W3C traceparent extracted, one span per database query named '<operation> <table>', logs bridged from tracing with trace and span ids (stdout logging stays), HTTP server request count and duration by method, route template and status (#731)
Web app: one span per user action of a flow and fetch spans that send traceparent to /api, exported to the same-origin /otlp path the Vite server forwards, development and E2E only (#732)

destinations.azure: API traces and logs to Application Insights appi-calendar-<suffix> through the Container Apps managed OpenTelemetry agent, configured in Bicep (#738); request metrics from Container Apps platform metrics; web telemetry not exported. Where to look: docs/runbooks/azure-infrastructure.md, Monitoring: where to look

allowed-attributes: opaque ids (trace, span, event or task UUID)
privacy.enforcement: An attribute filter in each SDK drops anything not allow-listed before export; a unit test per stack proves it

e2e-assertions: One trace per flow: browser span, API span(s) and database span(s) share one trace id with the flow's expected span names
Correlated logs: Loki holds the API's log records for the flow, carrying that trace id
Request metrics: Prometheus has the HTTP request count and duration series for the routes the flow hit
No personal data: none of the test's seeded values, the signed-in email, the session cookie or a token appears in spans, logs or metric labels
telemetry-decision.alerts-and-budgets: Not part of this control's decision; issue #80

metadata.runtime: Rust (toolchain pinned in backend/rust-toolchain.toml), axum on tokio, Diesel + diesel-async on tokio-postgres
metadata.tests: cargo test; API tests call the axum router in process with a fixed test clock on Testcontainers PostgreSQL (calendar-testing)
metadata.development-only: X-Dev-Seed-Key header scheme (Auth:DevSeedKey ≥ 32 chars) lets just db seed, and the Vite dev proxy under just frontend dev-signed-in, authenticate as the first allow-listed email

nodes.name: Calendar database (PostgreSQL 18)
nodes.description: The 'calendar' PostgreSQL database: users (keyed by Google's subject), events (owned by a user, with generated tstzrange/daterange spans and GiST indexes), tasks (owned by a user, with partial B-tree indexes led by owner_id for due and open-overdue lookups) and the session key (session_keys). Locally postgres:18.6-alpine in Docker Compose on 127.0.0.1:5432; in Azure a Flexible Server (Burstable Standard_B1ms, 32 GB, TLS required) per environment.

interfaces.privileges: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on tables; USAGE, SELECT on sequences; no DDL
Owns the database and schema; USAGE, CREATE on schema public; default privileges grant DML to calendar_app

data-durability.description: Managed backups with 7-day point-in-time retention in Azure, TLS-only transport, a narrow firewall, and database-level integrity constraints that mirror the domain rules (ADR-0014, ADR-0031).

config.engine: PostgreSQL 18 (image postgres:18.6-alpine locally and in Testcontainers; Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, version 18, in Azure)
config.storage: 32 GB; Burstable Standard_B1ms; staging is stopped when idle (no backups while stopped)
integrity-constraints: ck_tasks_due_date_xor_due_at: due_date IS NULL OR due_at IS NULL
ck_users_email_lower: email IS NULL OR email = lower(email); unique google_subject and email
fk_events_owner, fk_tasks_owner: owner_id REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT (ADR-0041)
Events: timed span tstzrange / all-day date_span daterange generated columns
xmin concurrency tokens on events and tasks
config.network-exposure: Local: bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Azure: public network access with firewall rules for the Container App outbound IPs and allow-listed operator IPs; require_secure_transport=on; private networking deferred (#84)

query-performance.description: Index design from the backend performance review (issues #50–#55): partial indexes for open/dated tasks, GiST range indexes for overlap queries, disjoint UNION ALL branches so partial indexes apply, and measured EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) plans in every query PR.

indexes: ix_tasks_due_date (owner_id, due_date) WHERE due_date IS NOT NULL
ix_tasks_due_at (owner_id, due_at) WHERE due_at IS NOT NULL
ix_tasks_completed_at (owner_id, completed_at) WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL
ix_tasks_open_due_date (owner_id, due_date) WHERE due_date IS NOT NULL AND completed_at IS NULL
ix_tasks_open_due_at (owner_id, due_at) WHERE due_at IS NOT NULL AND completed_at IS NULL

GiST on events.span (tstzrange) and events.date_span (daterange), single-column: the owner predicate is applied to the rows the overlap selects (btree_gist would need the Azure extension allow-list, ADR-0041)
config.overlap-strategy: Generated half-open ranges queried with && / @> through Diesel's range expression methods, because a B-tree on (start, end) cannot narrow start < X AND end > Y
config.overdue-strategy: Open and completed-within-today branches combined with Diesel's union_all (UNION ALL) so each matches its own partial index (queries::agenda::overdue_open and overdue_completed_within)
config.pagination-strategy: Keyset pagination with hand-expanded seek predicates around nullable keys (queries::task_list::for_view, endpoints/task_list_cursor.rs)
config.evidence: Seed ~100k realistic rows in a throwaway Testcontainers test, ANALYZE, then EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on the SQL Diesel generates; put before/after plans in the PR; never commit the harness
measured: Bulk complete of 50k tasks: 1.5 s set-based vs 40 s one by one

nodes.name: Database migrator
nodes.description: The only path that changes the schema: the calendar-migrate binary (backend/crates/calendar-migrate) applies the embedded SQL migrations as calendar_migrator, in one transaction under an advisory lock; on a database EF Core migrated it first records those migrations as applied. Locally `just db migrate`; in Azure `just infra migrate <env>` builds the binary and runs it, from the manually dispatched 'Database migration' GitHub Actions workflow. A failed run leaves the existing revision serving.

nodes.name: Infrastructure tool
nodes.description: .NET 10 file-based app (tools/infra) driven by the just infra module: `just infra what-if` and `just infra deploy <env> [foundation|full]` run the Bicep deployment with the Azure CLI, `just infra secret-init` stores the PostgreSQL admin password in the ops vault, `just infra init-roles` creates the database roles, `just infra db-stop` and `db-start` manage the staging server. Pinned Azure CLI and Bicep versions are verified by just doctor.

nodes.name: GitHub Actions (CI/CD)
nodes.description: Workflows in .github/workflows: CI (a Changes job that decides from the changed paths which jobs a pull request or merge group needs; backend, frontend, docs site, tooling, ADR conventions (the ADR check alone, for a change to the ADRs, story cards or model that runs no tooling job), Narratives (the narratives drift check alone, for a change to docs/narratives or the stitcher that runs no tooling job), container image + smoke test, cancelling a pull request's superseded runs, 'CI result'), CodeQL, dependency review, Infrastructure preview (Bicep what-if), Azure OIDC check, Database migration (manual, per environment, OIDC login) and Publish docs site (trusted workflow_run publisher for production and PR previews) and Dashboard snapshot (daily and on demand: takes and checks the delivery snapshot, commits it to the dashboard-data branch, and opens or updates the threshold issues; three jobs with separate permissions, never part of CI result).

delivery-performance.description: How long CI may make an author wait (ADR-0045, epic #380): each gated job of ci.yml fails a pull request when it is clearly slower than its pinned baseline, a daily trend check on main reports smaller slowdowns as one issue, and mechanism guards fail when the cause of a fixed slowdown (#272, #347, #368) comes back. The control points to the thresholds in .github/ci-baseline.json; it never copies them.

config.quantity: Each job's started_at to completed_at from the jobs API; queue time, skipped jobs, CI result and Cancel superseded runs are not gated

paths.publication: The Docs site step 'Build and verify publication artifact' succeeded: pushes to main and same-repository pull requests that run Docs site, i.e. that change the docs (ADR-0046)
paths.check: That step was skipped or Docs site did not run: dispatches and every other pull request

threshold.formula: ceil(max(exp(m + z * 1.4826 * MAD), M + max(floor, r * M))), m and MAD of ln(seconds), M = exp(m), z = Phi^-1(1 - alpha / J)

config.false-failure-budget: About 1 % of pull request runs with no regression, across all gated jobs (alpha / J per job, Bonferroni); back-tested on held-out runs with the observed rate and its one-sided 95 % upper bound in each baseline record. At the first pin (record 0014, 2026-11-07) 4 of 73 distinct runs, 5.5 %, would have failed with alpha = 1 %, accepted by the maintainer. Record 0017 (2026-11-08) recalibrated alpha to 0.1 % with Changes gated (J = 6): 0 of 136 held-out pull request runs fail (one-sided 95 % upper bound 2.2 %, still above the 1 % budget); a week of gated PR runs is reviewed in #421

baseline.update: Only by a deliberate pull request: regenerate the file with ci-timings --baseline and add a benchmark record in the same PR; runs on main never move it (docs/benchmarks/README.md, 'The pinned CI baseline')

gate.runs-in: A step of CI result, the single required check (ADR-0012), on the jobs API response that job already reads
reports-on: any run on a provisional path
gate.remedy: Re-run all jobs; Re-run failed jobs repeats only CI result on the same durations
gate.tests: tools/ci-timings/tests/GateTests.cs runs the committed jq program against canned jobs API responses, and checks that ci.yml runs that file
gate.critical-path-cost: CI result +3 s: median 6 s (n = 11) with the gate against 3 s (n = 23) without, measured in #395; the comparison itself takes 0 s, the rest is the sparse checkout and its post step. Accepted by the maintainer on 2026-11-07

trend-check.schedule: Daily at 06:23 UTC, and on demand
trend-check.test: One-sided Mann-Whitney U test of the last 20 successful push runs after the baseline against the publication-path baseline, per job
trend-check.minimum-effect: Hodges-Lehmann shift of at least max(10 s, 5 % of the baseline median)
trend-check.output: Opens, or comments on, the one open performance issue titled 'CI run-time trend: …'; never fails a run

mechanism-guards.mechanism: A same-repository pull request run has its own concurrency group, and Cancel superseded runs cancels the older runs with actions: write and no checkout
just tools test runs the test apps TOOLS_TEST_JOBS at a time, with a NuGet cache in the Tooling job
CI result always runs, needs every other job except Cancel superseded runs, and passes only when each succeeded or was skipped because the Changes job said the run does not need it
The docs loader lists the corpus once per sync, not once per document
The docs site is checked in its own Docs site job, and its typecheck reuses the build's sync
The web test suite runs one jsdom per worker
The Frontend job type-checks the web app once, and its build step is the bundler alone

A Changes job runs .github/ci-changes.jq on every run, and every other job but CI result and Cancel superseded runs needs it and runs only when its own output is true; ChangesRulesTests run the rules with jq

config.evidence: A delivery performance fix carries a test that fails when its mechanism is reverted and a benchmark record; a baseline change carries a record with the sample and the back-test; timings are asserted only through the pinned baseline

nodes.name: Delivery dashboard tool
nodes.description: .NET 10 file-based app (tools/delivery-dashboard) that gathers delivery data from the GitHub API (CI job run times against the pinned baseline and the ADR-0045 trend verdicts, queue time, the failure rates of CI jobs and reruns, pull request and issue flow, open stacks and epic progress) into one versioned, public-safe JSON snapshot per day. It validates every snapshot against the schema and the privacy rules (aggregates and public numbers only, no paths, handles or e-mail addresses) before it is published, checks the size of the data branch against its limit, and compares the snapshot with the thresholds, opening or updating one performance issue per kind of alert and no other alert.

flows.name: Google sign-in
flows.description: A signed-out person opens a deep link, signs in with Google, and comes back to the page they asked for with a same-origin session cookie. Only verified, allow-listed emails get a session (story 0005, ADR-0027).

transitions.description: The person opens a page such as /day/2026-10-29 in the browser
The app calls GET /api/auth/me; a 401 means no session, so it routes to /signin keeping the deep link as returnTo
'Sign in with Google' navigates to GET /api/auth/login?returnUrl=/day/2026-10-29 (503 if Google is not configured)
The API answers with an OIDC challenge; the browser is redirected to Google's authorization endpoint and the person signs in
Google redirects the browser back to /api/auth/callback/google with the authorization code

The API redeems the code for the ID token and claims, checks email_verified and the Auth:AllowedEmails allow-list, then finds or creates the person's users row by Google subject (the first allow-listed email claims the legacy-owner placeholder) and adds its id to the ticket (ADR-0041)
On success the API sets the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure session cookie (8 h) and redirects to the local returnUrl; on failure it redirects to /signin?error=access_denied without a session
The app calls GET /api/auth/me again (200: name, email, picture) and renders the header and the requested page

authentication.description: The flow must leave no session for a non-allow-listed or unverified email and must never follow a non-local return URL.

config.fallback-policy: CurrentUser extractor on every non-anonymous handler
config.open-redirect-protection: returnUrl validated as a local path on server and client; /signin itself is never a return target

metadata.not-automated: The real Google round trip, the denial redirect and the cookie/proxy settings are verified manually

transitions.description: The person opens / (today) or /day/$date; the router validates the date (1900–2200) and useToday(zone) follows the clock
useDayAgenda calls GET /api/agenda/day?date=YYYY-MM-DD&timeZone=Area/City with the browser's IANA zone ('+' encoded as %2B); cached data is shown meanwhile (keepPreviousData)

The API validates date and timeZone (400 problem details otherwise), computes the DST-correct DayWindow, opens one read-only REPEATABLE READ snapshot and runs the four range queries plus the overdue counts (overdue capped at 20)
Rows come back as plain Diesel row structs; endpoints/agenda_builder.rs buckets them into the days with the day-inclusion rules of calendar-domain and orders them (endpoints/agenda_order.rs)
200 DayAgendaResponse { date, timeZone, window, allDayEvents, events, tasks { overdue, overdueTotal, overdueOpenTotal, dueToday } }

The view renders in the viewer's zone with the now line, 'Past due' flags from the browser clock and 'View all N overdue'; it refetches on focus, every 5 minutes, at midnight and on manual Refresh, keeping the last data with a 'Couldn't refresh' notice on failure

read-consistency.description: One snapshot per agenda read so lists never disagree with each other.

time-correctness.description: The day shown is the client's local day in the client's zone; the server only computes the window.

config.instants: UTC DateTimeOffset with explicit offsets; floating dates as DateOnly

metadata.sibling: The week view (story 0002, ADR-0024) follows the same flow with GET /api/agenda/week?date&timeZone&today and a seven-day range

flows.name: Add an event
flows.description: From the day page the person adds a timed or all-day event in a modal dialog; the API validates and stores it, and the agenda views refetch. There is no optimistic insert (story 0004, story 0006, ADR-0057).

transitions.description: 'Add event' opens the native <dialog> prefilled with the viewed day (start at the next half hour or 09:00, end = start + 1 h); the browser zone is shown read-only; focus moves to the title

Client validation mirrors the server (title required ≤ 200, end after start, lengths); the DST resolver rejects a non-existent local time and asks which occurrence for an ambiguous one; an all-day event's inclusive last day becomes an exclusive endDate
POST /api/events with { title, allDay, start, end, timeZone | startDate, endDate, location, notes } (instants carry explicit offsets); the form is locked while saving

The API validates the timed/all-day field sets, builds CalendarEvent (UTC instants + IANA zone, or end-exclusive dates) and inserts it as calendar_app; the generated span/date_span columns index it for overlap queries

201 Created with Location /api/events/{id} and the EventResponse; 400 problem details map to fields (title, start/startDate, end/endDate, location, notes), other errors show form-level and keep the form open
The dialog closes, focus returns to 'Add event', a role=status message says e.g. 'Dentist added for Thu 29 Oct' with a Show day link, and the ['agenda'] queries are invalidated
The visible day or week agenda refetches (GET /api/agenda/day or /week) and now shows the event

metadata.sibling: Adding a task (stories 0003 and 0006) follows the same flow with POST /api/tasks { title, dueDate | dueAt, priority, notes }

flows.name: Edit or delete an event
flows.description: From the day page the person opens an event by its title, edits it in the event dialog or deletes it after a confirmation inside the dialog; updates are checked against the version the dialog loaded (story 0043, ADR-0052, ADR-0041).

transitions.description: The event's title (a button in All day or Schedule) opens the 'Edit event' dialog, which shows 'Loading event…'
GET /api/events/{id} (always fresh: the agenda has neither notes nor version)
200 EventResponse with version, shown in the browser zone (all-day as an inclusive last day); 404 'This event no longer exists.' and the agenda refreshes
Save: PUT /api/events/{id} with the create fields plus version. Delete event, then Delete: DELETE /api/events/{id}
The API loads the caller's event (query filter), applies the create rules, sets the expected xmin through RowVersion and saves; a stale version writes nothing
200 with the new version or 204; 400 field errors; 404 gone or another user's; 409 stale version

Success closes the dialog, says 'Dentist saved.' or 'Dentist deleted.', refetches ['agenda'] and returns focus to the title or the day heading; 409 reloads the latest version into the form and says the event was changed elsewhere; other errors keep the values for a retry

flows.name: Edit a task
flows.description: From the day page the person opens a task by its title (the checkbox still completes it), edits title, deadline, priority or notes in the task dialog, and saves against the version the dialog loaded (story 0044, ADR-0052, ADR-0041).

transitions.description: The task's title (a button; the checkbox is named by it) opens the 'Edit task' dialog, which shows 'Loading task…'
GET /api/tasks/{id} (always fresh: the agenda has neither notes nor version)
200 TaskResponse with version, a due instant shown as local date and time in the browser zone; 404 'This task no longer exists.' and the views refresh
PUT /api/tasks/{id} with { title, priority, notes, dueDate | dueAt | neither, version }

The API loads the caller's task (query filter), applies the create rules without touching completion, sets the expected xmin through RowVersion and saves; a stale version, including a complete or reopen since, writes nothing
200 with the new version; 400 field errors; 404 gone or another user's; 409 stale version

Success closes the dialog, shows 'Task saved.', refetches ['agenda'] and ['tasks'] and returns focus to the title, or to the day heading when the task left the day; 409 reloads the latest version into the form; other errors keep the values for a retry

flows.name: Tick a task off (optimistic)
flows.description: Ticking a task in any agenda or list updates the view immediately, calls the idempotent complete/reopen endpoint, rolls back only that task on failure, and refetches once after the last of a burst settles (stories 0001–0003, ADR-0052 concurrency).

transitions.description: The person ticks a task checkbox; that task is disabled while its own mutation is pending (useTaskTogglePending), not the whole list
useToggleTask.onMutate counts the in-flight toggle, cancels the view's query and patches the cached agenda/list (isCompleted, completedAt, overdueOpenTotal) through the view's TaskPatch adapter
POST /api/tasks/{id}/complete or POST /api/tasks/{id}/reopen
The API loads the task, applies the idempotent change (completedAt from the injected Clock) and saves with the xmin concurrency token
200 TaskResponse; 404 if the task is gone; 409 'The task was changed by another request' on a concurrency conflict

On error only that task is restored from the saved previous value and a message is shown; onSettled invalidates ['agenda'] and ['tasks'] when the last in-flight toggle settles or immediately after an error, so every view (day, week, My tasks) reconciles with the server

concurrency-control.description: Conflicting toggles are detected by xmin and reconciled by a refetch rather than overwritten.

config.client-behaviour: Per-task rollback, then invalidate agenda and task queries

flows.name: Triage all overdue tasks
flows.description: From 'View all N overdue' the person pages through every open overdue task and applies a bulk action (complete, reschedule, clear deadline, delete) to selected ids or to 'all N overdue' as a guarded set-based update (story 0007).

transitions.description: The day view or the week's Overdue panel shows 'View all N overdue' (agendas cap the list at 20 plus the totals); the person opens the lazy-loaded /triage route
GET /api/tasks?view=overdue&today=&timeZone=&limit= pages with opaque keyset cursors (limit 1–200, default 50); the first page carries the authoritative total
queries::task_list::for_view runs the keyset seek in SQL (local due date, due instant, id), fetching limit + 1 rows, and counts open overdue tasks for the first page
200 TaskPage { items, nextCursor, total }; rows show title, due value, priority and days overdue; notes load on demand (GET /api/tasks/{id})

The person selects ticked rows, 'Select all loaded' or 'Select all N overdue', picks an action and, for delete, confirms in a ConfirmDialog stating the count; a reschedule applies the DST rules (reject non-existent times, choose an ambiguous occurrence)
POST /api/tasks/bulk with { action, ids (chunks of ≤ 500) } or { action, filter: { view: overdue, today, timeZone, expectedTotal } }

Ids: load, apply per task (skipping deadline edits on completed tasks), save with xmin and report applied / skipped / notFound per id. Filter: SERIALIZABLE transaction, recount open overdue for today/timeZone, abort with 409 if it differs from expectedTotal, else one set-based UPDATE or DELETE
200 BulkTaskResponse { results[], applied, skipped, notFound } or 409 'The overdue task count changed' (also for serialization failures and deadlocks)
The UI reports what was skipped, asks the person to review the new count on 409, and invalidates the agenda queries so overdue counts and lists update on return

concurrency-control.description: 'All N overdue' must never act on a different set than the person saw.

config.strategy: Optimistic per id; SERIALIZABLE + expected-count guard for filtered writes

request-limits.description: Bulk and paging limits that bound a triage request.

metadata.measured: 50k tasks: bulk complete 1.5 s vs 40 s one by one; bulk delete 0.1 s vs 11 s
metadata.known-limitation: The count guard cannot detect a same-count swap

flows.name: Apply database migrations to an environment
flows.description: The operator dispatches the Database migration workflow for staging or production; it logs in to Azure with OIDC, reads the migrator credentials from the ops vault, builds the calendar-migrate binary and runs it as calendar_migrator, before any new app revision takes traffic (ADR-0052, ADR-0031, ADR-0034).

transitions.description: The operator dispatches 'Database migration' with the environment input (concurrency group migrate-<env>, GitHub environment <env> restricted to main)
The job verifies the PostgreSQL root certificates, installs the pinned Azure CLI, logs in with the federated identity (no stored secret) and runs just infra migrate <env>
The tool resolves the server host and reads calendar-migrator-password from the ops vault
cargo builds calendar-migrate, which runs against the environment's database as calendar_migrator over TLS; default privileges grant DML on any new table to calendar_app
The outcome is written to the job summary; a failed bundle stops promotion and the existing revision keeps serving

least-privilege-data-access.description: Schema changes happen only through this path and only as the schema owner.

privileges: Owner of the database and schema
config.migrations-applied-by: This workflow (Azure) or just db migrate (local); never the app

flows.name: Publish the decision log
flows.description: Merging to main (or opening a docs-only PR from this repository) builds the documentation site from the ADRs, story cards, architecture model, runbooks and benchmark records in CI and publishes it, or a PR preview, to GitHub Pages through a publisher that never runs untrusted code (ADR-0023, ADR-0025, ADR-0028).

transitions.description: A PR adds or changes an ADR, a story card, the architecture model, a runbook or a benchmark record (just tools adr and the docs tests pass locally) and is merged to main

The CI Docs site job builds the Astro Starlight site from docs/decisions, docs/stories, docs/architecture, docs/runbooks and docs/benchmarks, verifies it at the root path and at a project subpath, and uploads the docs-site artifact

After CI succeeds, the Publish docs site workflow's assemble job validates the source run, revision and PR state and that CI uploaded a publication artifact (only main pushes and docs-only PRs build one), downloads the exact artifact, assembles the retained production snapshot plus open-PR previews and uploads it; a separate deploy job deploys it with the github-pages environment, unless gh-pages has moved on to a later publication

The site is live at https://mgasca.github.io/calendar/ with each agent thought at agent-thoughts/NNNN/, each ADR at adr/NNNN/, each story at stories/NNNN/, each runbook at runbooks/<name>/ and each benchmark record at benchmarks/NNNN/; a docs-only PR gets an 'ADR preview' check and a sticky comment linking to pr-preview/pr-<number>/
